name: code-commandments
title: Code Commandments
description: The static code checker judges the codebase, its hooks run inside the journal, and every rule and language is a switch in its settings

aliases.name: sins
aliases.description: Judge the project against its commandments and show each sin as it is found

aliases.name: commandments-judge-changes
aliases.description: Judge what changed since the last commit against the project's commandments and show each sin as it is found

aliases.name: rules
aliases.description: Work on a rule of the project's own: try it on a path, prove it against the samples that mark it, or read a file's tree

aliases.name: commandments
aliases.description: Run any code-commandments verb through the binary this plugin fetched: report, info, repent, exemptions, make

curl.hint: curl fetches the checker's release binary into the plugin's own folder

python3.hint: python3, 3.9 or newer, runs the plugin's script for every event the journal hands it

sha256sum.hint: sha256sum or shasum checks the fetched binary against its release's SHA256SUMS

setup.name: Fetch the checker's release binary, checked against its SHA256SUMS
Write the chosen switches into config.json
Check for sins, on demand
setup.run: line="env JOURNAL_PLUGIN=code-commandments $JOURNAL_PLUGIN_DIR/bin/commandments-release judge"; id=$(journal check list | awk '/Check for sins/ { print $1; exit }'); if [ -n "$id" ]; then journal check edit "$id" --command "$line"; else journal check create "Check for sins" --command "$line" --every 0 --brief "Judges the whole project against its commandments; a failure lists each sin found, grouped by the skill that fixes it"; fi
